OPTIMIZING SHEET PILE PLACEMENT FOR SEEPAGE CONTROL AND SUSTAINABLE WATER MANAGEMENT IN NON-HOMOGENEOUS SOILS

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Ali Zuhair Abbas, Fadhel Abdulabbas Hassan
Print ISSN : 2523-5664
Online ISSN : 2523-5672

Doi: 10.26480/wcm.01.2026.362.370

ABSTRACT

This study examines the phenomenon of seepage beneath a hydraulic structure based on non-homogeneous soil. Various types of sandy soils were gathered from Najaf Governorate, Iraq, and arranged in three layers. The first layer consisted of fine gravel, the second layer was concrete sand (sand used in concrete production), and the third layer consisted of very fine sand (filter sand). The dimensions of the hydraulic structure model were adopted to be similar to those of the (Abu Sukhair Regulator) in Najaf.The experimental program considered various sheet pile slope angles of (45°, 60°, 90°, 135°, and 150°), as well as different sheet pile depths of 12, 24, and 36 cm. Furthermore, various numbers of sheet piles and different upstream water heads were studied.The results indicated that discharge and exit gradient values were considerably affected by the sheet pile inclination. The results also showed that the pore water pressure was negative (suction) in some cases, showing the development of suction pressure within the soil. The most significant improvement was observed when the angle of inclination was directed counterclockwise toward 45°. A notable reduction in seepage parameters was also noted when the sheet pile depth increased to 24 cm. However, increasing the number of sheet piles indicated no marked additional effect, and further increasing the depth to 36 cm did not result in a significant improvement. These results indicate that sheet pile direction and moderate penetration depth play a more significant role in seepage control than clearly increasing the number of sheet piles or using extreme penetration depth.
